candidates.title: Check accounting transaction accuracy

demandEvidence.chore: Building and checking accounting modules for transaction accuracy.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Campfire raised $65m and built an entire accounting module from scratch, they only managed to achieve ~95% accuracy rate. It might feel like 95% is very close to 100%, but that is not how it works.

ease.reason: A beginner could compare operator-supplied fictional transactions against fixed expected totals, but the post gives no implementation method or reference.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small accounting software teams may pay for transaction-checking support; this post establishes no service buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week prototype could flag discrepancies in synthetic transaction batches; reliable accounting coverage and production integration remain untested.

autonomy.reason: A proposed batch checker could repeat fixed comparisons, but humans must verify source records and every flagged transaction; no automation capability is documented.

evidence.reason: The post reports an accounting module build and its approximate accuracy, but does not describe a requested service, repeated workflow, inputs or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the post reports the challenge of building an accounting module and its accuracy, supporting only a narrow synthetic discrepancy-checking experiment; it does not establish an external request, recurring task or implementation capability.

rejected.title: Accounting software accuracy concern
rejected.reason: Below threshold after assessment: the discussion reports that a built accounting module reached about 95% accuracy, but supplies no implementation reference or direct service request. A synthetic discrepancy check is scorable, but the provisional criteria do not reach the threshold.

rejected.title: Amgi interface feedback
rejected.reason: The post says the software's UI is a downside, but gives no specific user task, requested redesign, or concrete chore. A workflow or paying customer cannot be grounded in this brief product critique.

rejected.title: Generic billing support prompt
rejected.reason: The captured text is only the forum template question, ‘What is the problem & what have you tried?’ It contains no actual billing issue or task evidence, so inferring a recurring billing-support workflow would invent demand.

steps.message: Reassessed the single feedback-named omission as a bounded synthetic transaction-checking experiment; its evidence and implementation limits keep it below threshold. The other two assigned discussion posts remain explicit evidence-based exclusions.
